passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the UnitedHealth Group third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. A question and answer session will follow UnitedHealth Group's prepared remarks. As a reminder, this call is being recorded. Here is some important introductory information. This call contains forward-looking statements under U.S. federal securities laws. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from historical experience or present expectations. A description of some of the risks and uncertainties can be found in the reports that we file with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including the cautionary statements included in our current and periodic filings. This call will also reference non-GAAP amounts. A reconciliation of the non-GAAP to GAAP amounts is available on the financial and earnings reports section of the company's investor relations page at www.unitedhealthgroup.com. Information presented on this call is contained in the earnings release we issued this morning and in our Form 8-K, dated October 13, 2026, which may be accessed from the investor relations page of the company's website. I will now turn the conference over to Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of UnitedHealth Group, Steve Hemsley.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Good morning, and thank you for joining us today. Our third quarter performance reflects actions taken throughout 2026, driving meaningful progress and reinforcing our confidence to sustainably grow in 2027 and beyond within our 13%-16% long-term target growth range. Our revised full-year 2026 guidance reflects continuing improvements in leadership and execution across Optum and UnitedHealthcare as we better align our businesses to serve the demands of the ever-changing U.S. healthcare environment. We are accelerating the modernization of our enterprise by advancing simplified and more responsive policies, processes, and tools, focusing on more effective integrated value-based care offerings, and responsibly building modern agentic infrastructure as we seek to ensure people have access to higher-quality care at lower costs, and at the same time, clinicians experience a simpler, faster, and more supportive system. Across the businesses, AI-enabled capabilities are beginning to help clinicians spend more time with patients, improve service speed and experience, streamline administration, and reduce friction for both consumers and clinicians. A few examples. We have expanded AI-enabled chart summarization to more than 40% of our employed clinicians, reducing chart review time by 33%. AI-enabled information gathering and research have shortened appeal cycle times by 26%, improving both member and clinician experience, and we expect this to

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: accelerate in 2027. For this year's Medicare Advantage annual enrollment period, we are introducing AI-powered plan recommendations that use a member's care history and local plan options to help simplify their selection. By the end of this year, we are on track to implement all previously announced prior authorization reforms, reducing decision timelines for patients, relieving administrative burden for clinicians, and delivering better experiences for people. Collectively, these initiatives will reduce total prior authorizations by 30%, including a reduction of two-thirds in prior authorizations for people under the age of 18. These efforts are only the beginning. More will follow. They are central to how we're changing our enterprise to be more in line with our mission, creating greater value and positive social impact. In that vein, an important effort is the reimagined United Health Foundation. With $1 billion committed to date, the foundation's investments, along with the dedicated operational expertise of UnitedHealthcare and Optum, can help facilitate scaled solutions to some of the U.S. health system's greatest challenges, including rural health, maternal and infant health, behavioral health, and workforce education. As just one example, in Tennessee, the foundation is helping expand and operate health hubs across the state, providing underserved communities with access to preventive care and chronic condition support. We will continue to highlight the foundation

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: as part of our commentary on our earnings calls going forward. The broader healthcare environment remains dynamic. Policy-driven regulatory developments, changing consumer expectations, and the rapid evolution of clinical care and advances in technology continue to reshape the industry. These factors are pressuring basic affordability and access as never before. Success requires continuous adaptation, and the pace is accelerating. We recognize this and remain restless in our pursuit of change and improvement. We are challenging our assumptions, revising policies and practices, and repositioning leadership and capabilities to better meet the needs of those we serve and to move faster as an enterprise to adapt to the changing healthcare landscape. That includes opportunities to better align with clinical partners, employers, and government benefit sponsors to help improve the experience of all stakeholders in healthcare. We've made progress in our 2026 performance. We have much to do to approach the full potential of our mission and the positive impact we can make as an enterprise. UnitedHealth Group has a long history of evolution to meet the needs of a changing U.S. health system. We're committed to accelerating these efforts as a stronger, more capable, more mission-centered enterprise. With that, let me turn the call over to Tim Noel.

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare: Thanks, Steve. UnitedHealthcare is seeing positive momentum across our Medicare and Medicaid businesses, while our commercial business continues to adjust to a challenging but steadily stabilizing environment. Costs remain stubbornly high across the entire healthcare landscape, and particularly in areas such as specialty pharmacy and acute healthcare service intensity. We continue to address the challenge of increasingly expensive care with appropriate medical management, operational discipline, and a commitment to identify and remove excess and unnecessary costs from our own enterprise as we advance simpler and more modern services. We are working to deliver stable benefits and value for our members and customers. We believe this positions us for continued organic growth and long-term value creation entering 2027. Let me start with our Medicare business, where the annual enrollment period begins later this week. Medicare Advantage remains the choice of well more than half of eligible American seniors as it offers better and more modern benefits, and importantly, better outcomes than fee-for-service Medicare. Beneficiaries choosing Medicare Advantage save on average more than $4,000 annually through lower premiums and cost sharing than those on original Medicare. With adequate funding, we believe Medicare Advantage will continue to be the choice of American seniors, particularly those who are disadvantaged and have chronic care challenges as

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: they seek better value and modern care. Heading into 2026, we made deliberate decisions regarding Medicare Advantage benefit design and market positioning to preserve the long-term sustainability and performance of our Medicare Advantage offerings. We continued this disciplined approach for 2027. We believe we are competitively positioned, focused on providing value for seniors in the markets we serve while being mindful of trend dynamics. In 2027, UnitedHealthcare will continue to prioritize high-value HMO, chronic special needs, and dual special needs offerings. Our commitment to serving America's seniors is clear. More than 94% of Medicare-eligible individuals nationwide will have access to a UnitedHealthcare Medicare plan, and approximately 90% of Medicare-eligible consumers will have access to one of our Medicare Advantage plans with a $0 premium option. We are maintaining important benefits such as dental, vision, hearing, and additional health and wellness offerings that make a real difference in the lives of seniors. UnitedHealthcare chronic special needs plans will be available to nearly 50 million Medicare-eligible individuals in 2027, providing specialized support for people living with conditions such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and chronic heart failure. These plans offer benefits and access to care tailored to the unique needs of individuals managing chronic conditions, helping them connect with care, medications, and support they need. Much of this

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: work is in coordination with our partners at Optum Health, where evidence shows chronically complex seniors served by integrated value-based care experience better preventive care while improving health outcomes at lower costs. Medicare Advantage patients in value-based care arrangements are 40% less likely than traditional Medicare patients to be hospitalized for acute and chronic conditions, and 40% less likely to be readmitted to a hospital within 30 days of discharge. Moving to Stars. Our initial Star Ratings for payment year 2028 reflect our investment in quality, member experience, and operating execution. As we move through 2027 and into 2028, we expect to approach 75% of total members in four-plus Star plans compared to the industry average of 70%. Our team remains intensely focused on building a best-in-class consumer and clinical experience. Along with better benefit design and stability going forward, we believe those efforts will continue translating into stronger quality performance over time. We will continue to work in support of the CMS quality program efforts to ensure the Medicare Advantage program continues to provide a quality experience and stability to the 36 million seniors who depend on it. Turning to medical costs. The actions we've taken to improve and modernize care management, strengthen clinical engagement, and enhance operating discipline are having a meaningful effect. Care intensity remains elevated relative to historical norms, even as we

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: continue to see signs that trends are bending in a more stable direction than what we have recently experienced. We remain respectful of trends and are not assuming any deceleration to historical patterns or to ongoing clinician pricing pressure. Demand for care remains strong, particularly among senior and complex populations, and we fully support appropriate access to care for our members. Turning to the commercial business. Performance continues to stabilize as we navigate a challenging market. As we previously noted, trends for commercial benefits are exceeding our initial expectations of 11%, driven by an acceleration of costs related to the No Surprises Act, greater cost intensity from clinicians, and high-cost specialty drugs. Of particular concern is the ongoing abuse of the No Surprises Act dispute process by a relatively small number of clinician groups and third-party organizations. Arbitration awards can approach nearly 6% of total medical spend in some regions, translating to billions of dollars in excess costs for consumers, employers, and the health system. The law was intended to protect patients from unexpected bills, and we strongly support that objective. We will continue working with policymakers and regulators to ensure the law functions as intended and that healthcare dollars are directed toward appropriate patient care rather than significantly inflated market arbitration awards and volumes, along with unnecessary administrative expense. Medicaid

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: remains stable through the back half of the year, while our team continues to drive greater operational improvements through network curation and more effective behavioral health program initiatives. These actions help to partially offset the primary variable, which continues to be the timing and adequacy of state funding across several markets. As we move through the balance of 2026, we continue to work collaboratively with our state partners to ensure rates appropriately reflect the acuity and healthcare needs of the families being served, including the impacts of regulatory actions. While progress has been made in many states, the timing of updates remains uneven. Based on our current outlook, we continue to view 2026 as a trough year for core Medicaid margins, which we now expect to be moderately better than negative 1%. Finally, we are focusing intensely on enhancing our support for, and relationships with, clinicians and health systems. In addition to the prior authorization changes Steve mentioned, which we see as only the beginning, we are meaningfully speeding up our claims processing and payments, and re-energizing our relationship engagement efforts with more dedicated resources and executive ownership. Our goal is to provide a more seamless experience for clinicians and health systems who work with us and to resolve issues more quickly. As we look toward 2027 and beyond, we are shifting our focus to sustainable organic growth underpinned by improving Medicare

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: fundamentals, a stronger commercial outlook, continued opportunities to enhance Medicaid performance, and an organization that is operating with greater discipline and accountability for all our stakeholders. With that, I'll turn it over to Patrick.

passages.heading: Patrick, Optum Executive
passages.text: Patrick, Optum Executive: Thanks, Tim. Our results from the third quarter underscore the important work underway across all of Optum to lay the groundwork for long-term growth. Starting with Optum Health. Overall, Optum Health continued to deliver strong performance in the third quarter, driven by the continued return to value-based care principles, combined with strong execution across our clinical programs and operational improvements, enabling clinicians to focus more on their patients and improve patient experience. A few examples for this morning: a 27% increase from last year in online self-scheduling, making it easier for patients to reach clinicians; and an increase in home health visits by 10% over last year. We are very encouraged by the early success of our program to co-locate behavioral specialists within our primary care practices. The number of patients referred has doubled since last year, with an engagement rate of more than 90%. As Tim mentioned, it is now more important than ever to provide seamless care and coverage for our chronic and complex patients through all phases of the care continuum, from primary care to specialist, to home, to the pharmacy. Moving to Optum Rx. Our focus in this business continues to be on two efforts to ensure value alignment to the customers and patients we serve. First, we continue to increase transparency on the PBM side of Optum Rx. Through the 2027 selling season, we have seen our industry-first affordability, experience,

passages.heading: Patrick, Optum Executive
passages.text: and transparency initiatives resonating in the marketplace and with customers. The employers, governments, and unions we serve continue to recognize the vital role of PBMs in controlling prescription drug costs and ensuring people have access to the medications they need, particularly as the prices charged by drug manufacturers continue to increase. For the first time, over 50% of Optum Rx membership is external, non-UHC membership. Second, we fundamentally believe that pharmacy services have to be closer to the patient. Accordingly, you will see continued efforts within our separate pharmacy services businesses to more closely align pharmacy care with medical care. Integrated value-based care means just that: integrated. When pharmacy care and medical care are aligned, outcomes improve for the patients we serve, access improves, and the total cost of care is lowered. Specifically, within the pharmacy service side of Optum Rx, Genoa continues to expand its dedicated behavioral health pharmacy footprint and serve patients with serious mental illness and substance use disorders. Specialty pharmacy continues to grow through both volume and mix while improving patient support for increasingly complex therapies. Infusion services are becoming more important as we help shift appropriate care into lower-cost and more convenient settings. We will continue to expand our portfolio of integrated pharmacy services and align them as close to medical care settings as possible, delivering

passages.heading: Patrick, Optum Executive
passages.text: better care, convenience, and access. Turning to Optum Insight. 2026 has been both a performance and an investment year, and 2027 will show meaningful progress, setting the foundation for accelerating growth in 2028 and beyond. Our investment focus has been on further developing and bringing to market healthcare-specific AI solutions that enhance productivity and performance outcomes while improving the patient and clinician experience. Overall, we are looking to 2027 with confidence. Our major remediation work is largely complete, and it's created a strong foundation for growth across Optum. With that, I'll turn it over to Wayne.

passages.heading: Wayne, CFO
passages.text: Wayne, CFO: Thanks, Patrick, and good morning. Third quarter results reflect continued progress across the enterprise and improving execution in our businesses where we have been focused on operating reforms to drive better consumer and clinician experience. For Q3 2026, we reported revenue of $113 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $4.69, up from $2.92 a year ago. Consolidated medical care ratio of 88.4% for the quarter compares to 89.9% last year. The quality of earnings is strong and durable as we head into 2027. At UnitedHealthcare, performance continued to reflect pricing discipline, fundamental medical cost management, and care delivery enhancements. We continue to be respectful of elevated utilization trends, which typically step up in the back half of the year, particularly in our risk-based businesses. Within Optum Health, we are seeing steady progress from modernization, a return to a disciplined value-based care approach, and operating improvements as the actions taken through 2026 begin to yield results. In Optum Insight, performance is benefiting from technology and AI-enabled improvements, including payment integrity and broader operating efficiency, while we invest in new areas to expand and modernize our offerings to drive growth. In Optum Rx, we continue to see the benefits of disciplined execution and the breadth of our pharmacy services model, now based on a simpler, more transparent approach to serving these evolving market needs. Turning to the

passages.heading: Wayne, CFO
passages.text: full year, our updated 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of at least $20.50 reflects performance through the third quarter, balanced by expected investments in the final months of the year. From a capital deployment perspective, our priorities remain consistent. First, reinvest in the business through targeted organic growth and steady expansion in care delivery, technology, modernization, and broad-based AI adoption. Second, maintain balance sheet strength. Third, return value to shareholders. Our balance sheet remains strong. Our debt-to-capital ratio was 41.7% at the close of the quarter, and we remain on track to approach 40% by year-end. We repurchased $5 billion of UNH stock through the third quarter. We have paid $6.2 billion in dividends year to date and expect to exceed $8 billion by year-end. Our strategic priorities remain focused on capabilities that align with and strengthen our ability to deliver value to consumers, benefit sponsors, and customers, and support long-term growth for shareholders. We view our 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of at least $20.50 as a solid run rate on which to grow. We would offer that current analyst consensus for 2027 may understate the opportunity ahead, and we see the lower end of our long-term 13%-16% growth rate as a more reasonable starting point. As we think about 2027 more broadly, we continue to see a balanced set of tailwinds and headwinds. Tailwinds include continued enterprise-level performance progress, share repurchases,

passages.heading: Wayne, CFO
passages.text: value-based care performance improvements, and further gains from AI and modernization that improve both consumer and clinician experiences, drive productivity benefits, reduce costs, and create sustainable performance improvement opportunities for our business and those we serve, as well as product opportunities for Optum Insight. On the headwind side, we will accelerate our investments in the policy reforms and modernization of the businesses, particularly in UnitedHealthcare and Optum Insight, and remain respectful of medical trends and the broader external environment where health benefit funding remains pressured. Overall, we're steadily and methodically improving performance broadly across the portfolio. We are positioned to finish 2026 strongly, and we remain focused on consistently delivering our 13%-16% long-term growth target. With that, I'll turn it back over to Steve.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Thanks, Wayne. Let me close with a few thoughts before we move to questions. For a little more than a year, our priorities have been clear. Return to our core mission and culture. Better serve the needs of healthcare as one enterprise and one leadership team. Restore financial and operating discipline. Turn around and strengthen our performance business by business across all performance measures. Begin the process of reimagining and modernizing all we do to harness the compelling potential of modern intelligent technologies. Simplify our processes, elevate our service levels, and advance our response and service speed to consumers and clinicians. Finally, reposition all our businesses to return to responsible levels of profitable organic growth. As you've heard today, we are well underway in all those areas. But fully achieving those priorities requires us to get outside our four walls.

passages.heading: Patrick, Optum Executive
passages.text: Patrick, Optum Executive: Throughout our company, we are spending time listening carefully to customers, consumers, clinicians, policymakers, and other stakeholders. We're doing so with humility and with a service mindset, conscious of the positive role we can play and the responsibility we have to improve the health system experience when we operate at our best.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Those conversations are helping renew and reinforce the fundamental understanding that success in healthcare depends on relationships and trust, and we need to continue to build both with all stakeholders. We will continue listening, we will continue learning, and we will continue advancing our business in ways that improve experiences, provide easier access, and lower costs while delivering better outcomes. For you, our shareholders, all these accountabilities align and create value. The progress we've made in 2026 gives us confidence. Our businesses are improving. Our modernization efforts are gaining traction. Our investments in AI and in integrated value-based care are creating tangible benefits today while positioning us for the future. We remain focused on better managing our businesses, finishing 2026 strong, and building that foundation for growth in 2027 and 2028 and beyond. We look forward to providing you a more comprehensive update on our outlook for next year before year-end. I will thank you now, and, Operator, let's open the line for questions.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: The floor is now open for questions. At this time, if you have a question or comment, please press star one on your touch-tone phone. You may remove yourself from the queue by pressing star two on your touch-tone phone. We ask you to limit yourself to one question. If you ask multiple questions, we will only be answering the first question so that we can respond to everyone in the queue this morning. Our first question comes from Justin Lake with Wolfe Research.

passages.heading: Justin Lake, Analyst
passages.text: Justin Lake, Analyst: Thanks. Good morning. I wanted to focus on the government side for a second, specifically your comments around Medicaid. Things were getting better. I am curious what you are seeing in terms of your third-quarter run rate and what is driving that. Are you actually back to kind of break-even given your improvement there? Maybe you can also let us know where your MA margins are at this point for 2026. Thanks.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Mike, do you want to take that?

passages.heading: Mike, Executive, Medicaid
passages.text: Mike, Executive, Medicaid: Sure. Thanks, Justin. Good morning, and thank you for the question. As Tim Noel indicated, our membership and overall Q here are within our expectations, and we now expect full 2026 performance moderately better than our forecasted range. The main drivers of that activity have really been our focus on complex care cost management, network and services curation, increasing our membership engagement, particularly in our AI-powered coaching activities, modernization activities, and the ongoing identification and removal of fraud, waste, and abuse. We do believe these activities are doable. We did see good improvement in Q3, and we believe that will continue for the rest of the year. We continue to see elevated trends in the areas of behavioral healthcare services, specialty pharmacy services, and home and community-based services, and also in inpatient care costs as well. Those elevated rates are moderating slightly, and we're continuing to monitor that. We anticipate margin improvement as we look into next year, and we will continue to work with our state partners to mitigate what has been a stubborn gap between funding and medical cost trends through the year. Again, as we think about this for 2028, we're very aspirational to move to targeted margins by the end of that year. Thank you for the question.

passages.heading: Bobby, Medicare Executive
passages.text: Bobby, Medicare Executive: Hey, Justin, maybe this is Bobby on the Medicare margin piece that you highlighted. Given where we've paced through 2026, we do now expect to be near the top end of the 2%-4% range. I would attribute a lot of that to some of the great recovery actions that the team has executed throughout the year. Think about the initiatives around medical trend, our cost management focus, and then a broader focus on the durable product offerings that we've brought to the marketplace for 2026. It also allows us to make investments now to set us up for future success. Think about what we're doing in quality, AI, modernization, and providers. Ultimately, I feel good about how it sets us up for continued success in 2027. Thanks for the question.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Thanks. Next question, please.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Lance Wilkes with Bernstein.

passages.heading: Lance Wilkes, Analyst
passages.text: Lance Wilkes, Analyst: Great. Could you talk a little bit about how you are approaching growth in 2027, in particular in Medicare Advantage as you are approaching the top end of the range, how you are looking at growth there? Likewise, with the selling seasons in for national accounts and for PBM, how is that coming along?

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: We will start with Bobby.

passages.heading: Bobby, Medicare Executive
passages.text: Bobby, Medicare Executive: Yep. Yeah. Hey, thanks, Lance, for the question. Yes, AEP is right around the corner here. We will wait until later this year to provide formal membership guidance. Maybe a couple of early observations to share with you. Obviously, some of the things we did as we set out for planning in 2027 was continue to look at ensuring we have a durable set of product offerings, and that meant some continued footprint refinements and product refinements, really around the residual PPOs that we started moderating a year or two ago. Then as I look at the opportunities, I think there is actually a lot of good growth potential out there. Maybe one important statistic for you: even with some of the footprint refinements, we did actually expand our overall footprint. Tim noted it in the prepared remarks. Now more than 94% of American Medicare eligibles have access to one of our plan offerings. That is an expansion year over year. We also took a more dynamic approach to the product planning this year, and I think there are some real opportunities for smart, durable growth in the marketplace right now. We are particularly focused on the D-SNP offerings, the C-SNP offerings, and then some of the high-value HMO plans. I think we are better positioned to capture that growth in some of those key areas as we step into AEP in 2027 than we have been in recent years, and we aligned our go-to-market strategy accordingly. Maybe just one last thing to highlight on that is when I

passages.heading: Bobby, Medicare Executive
passages.text: think about the overall capabilities of the enterprise, the capabilities that we bring to bear, and our emphasis on value-based care, I do think we have an incredible opportunity to make an impact for the members who are on these D-SNP, C-SNP, and HMO plans, and really drive some incredible outcomes and quality for those folks over time.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Great. Thanks, Bobby.

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare: Yeah. Lance, this is Tim Noel. I am going to turn it over to Brandon Cuevas, who is our new CEO of our commercial business, for some insights into the commercial selling season and our pricing posture there.

passages.heading: Brandon Cuevas, CEO, Commercial Business
passages.text: Brandon Cuevas, CEO, Commercial Business: No, thanks, Lance. Appreciate the question. We're coming off of two really strong years in national account sales, and we're pleased to see that our persistency and our group retention look very strong going into 2027. As we look at our pipeline and our selling season, we're well through that in our national accounts base, and we've had a really successful selling season this year. I think as we think about the overall growth looking into our commercial business, again, I think we remain respectful of trend. We've had to be very mindful of the trend increases as well as being remarkably focused on affordability. As we look at 2026, we think that our growth is going to be reflective of some of the increased trend pressures that we've seen in the marketplace. Our pipeline filling and products like Surest, and where we are in our mid-market selling, are actually continuing to come in remarkably strong. So we're having a very solid selling season looking at 2027. But we're still in the midst of our mid-market selling, while national accounts look very strong going into next year. Thanks for the question.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Thanks, Brandon. How about John on PBM?

passages.heading: John, Optum Rx Executive
passages.text: John, Optum Rx Executive: Yeah, thank you, Steve, and Lance, thank you for the question. Building really on Brandon's comments, we've enjoyed a couple of strong selling seasons in back-to-back years, and we see that trend continuing this year, really driven by the transformation and transparency modernization efforts within the PBM. Those efforts are really resonating in the market, driven first and foremost by the fact that every Optum Rx client gets the benefit of the fully transparent supply chain instrumentation that we are putting in place. So that's driving retention again in the high 90s this year, and then success in the new client marketplace, as Patrick mentioned in his prepared remarks. While maintaining pricing discipline, we're growing membership now to north of 50% of our covered lives and expect that trend to continue in 2027. As we wind down the year, we're staying close to our clients who are in the heat of the enrollment season. Brandon and I still have efforts in flight together. We'll stay close to those clients as we work to update our membership outlook for 2027. Thanks for the question.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Great. Thank you. Next question, please.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Stephen Baxter with Wells Fargo.

passages.heading: Stephen Baxter, Analyst
passages.text: Stephen Baxter, Analyst: Yeah. Hi, thanks. Just to round out some of the 2027 color, I think you just spoke pretty clearly to the health plan and PBM assumptions. Can you add some color on how you're thinking about your top-line dynamics for Health and Insight and repositioning those businesses for growth, I think, in 2028 or beyond? Thanks.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Sure. We'll start out with Krista, and then we'll go to Sandeep.

passages.heading: Krista, CEO, Optum Health
passages.text: Krista, CEO, Optum Health: Yeah. Thanks so much for the question, Stephen. I want to just start with highlighting some of the performance that we're actually seeing inside the third quarter. Really strong performance in our clinical programs and in medical management. Those programs are going to continue to be durable as we head into 2027. The work we're doing to reduce unnecessary inpatient stays, the work we're doing to improve access to primary care and preventive care, and the work we're also doing to improve access to home health and help serve our patients in community and home settings. As I think about 2027, again, we'll unpack more of this in the coming months, but I think we're really confident in our ability to grow earnings inside 2027. Our focus is going to be on just really thoughtful growth. There are a couple of things I maybe would just point to as growth opportunities for this business in 2027, but also just really long term. First is that we serve 20 million patients today. About 4 million of those are in fully accountable relationships. So there's still room for fully accountable growth, but even more importantly, lots of opportunity for professional capitation, shared savings, and other ways in which we can serve our patients in our integrated model. Second, I would point to the high-performing service lines that we have today. Think of examples like home health, hospice, surgery centers, D-SNP, C-SNP, and HMOs. Again, lots of opportunity for growth in

passages.heading: Krista, CEO, Optum Health
passages.text: those services to go deeper in our existing markets and serve more patients more comprehensively. Last, I would also point to opportunities where we're launching new products in the market. Maybe just calling out one as an example. This year, in partnership with one of our payers, we've expanded our ability to manage risk across a post-acute continuum. So think from an inpatient hospital stay all the way through SNF and home health. We've seen really strong demand for these products to serve post-acute care risk comprehensively, and we're also really pleased with the results. We're seeing improved access to timely care, again, improved access to home health utilization, and I think you'll see those programs also expand inside 2027. So, taken together, this is still a multi-year journey to make sure we're pacing appropriately toward our 6%-8% target margin range, but we see ample opportunity for growth inside Optum Health.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: You are really oriented to the new.

passages.heading: Krista, CEO, Optum Health
passages.text: Krista, CEO, Optum Health: Exactly.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: The new things.

passages.heading: Krista, CEO, Optum Health
passages.text: Krista, CEO, Optum Health: Exactly.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Sandeep.

passages.heading: Sandeep, CEO, Optum Insight
passages.text: Sandeep, CEO, Optum Insight: Stephen, for Optum Insight, the goal is to simplify healthcare with AI for consumers, providers, payers, and life sciences companies. As 2026 is on plan, I want you to think about Insight as a multi-year investment and execution journey. There are a few moving parts here. We are continuing to rationalize existing products and contracts where they do not make sense. We are infusing AI into our existing offerings that help make them more competitive and profitable, then launching new AI-first products and platforms. To give you some examples of the momentum there, our Optum AI consulting firm, with a Medicaid plan, is helping them adjudicate their most complex claims in seconds instead of days using agentic AI. Another example is a product called Optum Integrity One, which automates claims coding in the revenue cycle space. We launched this at the end of 2025. We had two clients at the end of 2025. Today, we have 15 clients implemented and another 24 clients implementing. You see the momentum of some of our new AI clients. We recently launched a partnership joining the Anthropic Partner Network. We had announced similar go-to-market partnerships with Microsoft and Google in recent quarters across products. We are seeing strong, disciplined execution, new team members who are AI-first, and new product teams, et cetera. In the next two quarters, we will be seeing a series of product launches. Overall, with those moving parts, we feel confident about

passages.heading: Sandeep, CEO, Optum Insight
passages.text: our prospects for 2027. Thank you.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: AI is reinventing that business. Next question, please.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: We will take our next question from A.J. Rice with UBS.

passages.heading: A.J. Rice, Analyst
passages.text: A.J. Rice, Analyst: Thanks. Hi, everybody. I might go back to the commercial business. I think the risk portion, you guys have indicated that maybe that is operating at a below 5% margin. Part of that is the IDR issues that you have highlighted. It sounds like you are saying today that that is stabilizing somewhat, and I know that historically you have talked about that business having a high single-digit, 7%-10% or something margin. I wonder your thoughts about the pacing of margin recovery there, and maybe flush out a little bit more about the stabilization you are seeing right now.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Tim, do you want to start with that?

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare: Yeah. Thanks, A.J. Good morning. As we talked about in the opening remarks, we are seeing a stabilization of the trends that we're seeing, the medical cost trends in the commercial business, albeit at levels that are high and significantly higher than historical norms that we've seen in the commercial business. As we priced for 2027, we took the view that we would see these trends continue and persist into 2027 and priced rationally, consistent with all of that. As we think about our long-term targeted margins and some of these utilization pressures that we're facing in the commercial business, it is going to stretch out our ability to achieve those long-term objectives and margins for the commercial business. More color in a couple of months. We'll have an opportunity to dive into some of the detail of that business, but that's how you should be thinking about it right now.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Thank you. Next question, please.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Ann Hynes with Mizuho Securities.

passages.heading: Ann Hynes, Analyst
passages.text: Ann Hynes, Analyst: Great. Thank you. Maybe we could fine-tune some of your earlier comments on MA. Just in general, how do you view your competitiveness from a benefit offering versus your peers? Do you believe UNH is positioned to deliver overall membership growth for next year? Thanks.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Bobby?

passages.heading: Bobby, Medicare Executive
passages.text: Bobby, Medicare Executive: Yeah. Hey, Ann. Thanks for the follow-up question. We are not going to get to specific guidance. We will get to that here in a few months. That said, we took a very deliberate approach for 2025 with a focus on investing in benefits, investing in products, and providing stability in products where we know we can make a meaningful impact on growth, a meaningful impact on the consumers that we serve, and a meaningful impact in partnership with many of our value-based care providers who serve those populations. Think about that again in the context of our D-SNP, our C-SNP, and our HMO plans. A big part of why we have had the recovery actions we have in 2026 is our focus in those areas, the broad capabilities that we bring to life in those areas, our ability to get after some of the medical cost areas, driving more cost management, things of that nature. I think as I look to 2027 and look at the competitive landscape, we have a nice opportunity to capture some of that growth to continue serving more members in those areas, and that is what we are focused on as we continue to modernize our business. Thanks for the question.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Next question, please.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: We will take our next question from Kevin Fischbeck with Bank of America.

passages.heading: Kevin Fischbeck, Analyst
passages.text: Kevin Fischbeck, Analyst: Great, thanks. I appreciate the earlier comments that trend tends to be a little bit higher in the back half of the year, but the trend data points that we are tracking really imply that trends start off really low to start the year, but have accelerated as the year has gone on. Is this consistent with what you are seeing? If so, why is it maybe accelerating a little bit more than normal? I guess how comfortable are you that you are repricing 2027 to the exit rate as far as trend goes? Thanks.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Tim?

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare: Yes. Good morning, Kevin. This is Tim. We are not seeing the dynamics that you are talking about. When you go across each of our businesses, we have talked about commercial continuing at the level, stabilizing somewhat in more recent durations, but still tracking north of 11%. We talked about seeing moderation in trend in the Medicaid business. We are seeing some better-than-expected performance when you start thinking about the Medicare businesses broadly. But in terms of trend acceleration, no, we are not seeing that. In fact, we are seeing some moderation in the government programs business and stabilization in the commercial business. As we think about our forward pricing, right now we are able to incorporate the latest information using better analytical tools, more real-time information on the direction of travel of medical cost utilization, and are incorporating all of that into our forward pricing assumptions, but not seeing the elevation that you are referencing as we pace through the year.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Thank you. Next question, please.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Scott Fidel with Goldman Sachs.

passages.heading: Scott Fidel, Analyst
passages.text: Scott Fidel, Analyst: Hi, thanks. Good morning. I was hoping, just on the Medicaid side, to hear your thinking around, if we think about 2027 to 2030, and you have that natural opportunity for cyclical margin recovery in Medicaid, clearly with margins still negative, then having to interface with the implementation of the OBBB reforms that will scale up from 2027 to 2030. Maybe walk us through how you see those two offsetting each other, and maybe how you think about a reasonable view on where margins may average over that time period. Thanks.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Mike?

passages.heading: Mike, Executive, Medicaid
passages.text: Mike, Executive, Medicaid: Scott, thanks for the question. Lisa, as we look at what's happening over the next four years, there certainly will be a cycle process that goes through the Medicaid business. We've seen this over history, if you look at it, and we expect that to happen through Medicaid for this cycle as well, particularly as we think about OBBB. We think there is an opportunity to get back to rate-level margins in 2028. We're continuing to focus on our efforts around clinical care management, cost management, and leveraging AI tools to do that as well. We do think that over time there will be opportunities for us to look at markets, to look at ways we can tie into our strategy around duals and make sure that this can be effective.

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare: But overall, we think getting back to those margins and remaining at those margins will be an opportunity for us and will be our goal through 2030. Thank you for the question.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: In the long term, Medicaid is a good, durable marketplace that will continue to grow. Next question, please.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Gill with JPMorgan.

passages.heading: Lisa Gill, Analyst
passages.text: Lisa Gill, Analyst: Thanks very much. I had a question on specialty pharmacy. You brought it up on the cost side, but Patrick also talked about it on the opportunity side. I just really want to understand two things here. One, you talked about infusion. I am curious about capabilities today and what you see around infusion. Two, what do you see around potential opportunities in biosimilars? Then lastly, the comment around integrated medical and pharmacy together. You talked about the fact that 50% are now external clients. I am curious about how you bring the two entities together if they are not under a single umbrella of UnitedHealth Group.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Sure. Why don't we start with Patrick, and then we will go to John, and then we might come back to Patrick on the integrated piece. Okay?

passages.heading: Patrick, Optum Executive
passages.text: Patrick, Optum Executive: Look, Lisa, thanks for the question. We will call out a few areas. First, specialty pharmacy, as you know well with the drug pipeline and the patient need, is a growing market. What we talked about in the opening comments is we are increasingly bringing that closer and closer with our care delivery enterprise and clinicians broadly across the marketplace. John and the team have led terrific efforts both in LDD drugs, where we have high win rates with care models, working with Krista and the Optum Health team, and also working with external clinicians and physicians and prescribers. We see that market continuing to grow, and it is about service, experience, and patient care. Infusion, you also alluded to. That is a lower-cost setting, as you know, and more convenient for patients. What we hear from payers and our other customers is they want infusion to grow because it is lower cost and a better experience for patients. Once again, we have a robust clinical care model and growth in that area. I will let John talk a little bit more about the PBM and pharmacy linkage, and then we will go from there.

passages.heading: John, Optum Rx Executive
passages.text: John, Optum Rx Executive: Yeah, very good. Thank you, Patrick. I'll start, Lisa, with the strength within. Patrick started with this. The strength within our specialty pharmacy is led by Michael Einodshofer and the team. We're winning on experience there, Lisa. If you look at overall volumes, while volumes might have been down 5% for the quarter, specialty volumes were actually up 2.6% for the quarter, and that's driven by a couple of initiatives. We're winning on provider choice, which again is strong LDD win rates, our strongest in years there, Lisa, coupled with the continued build-out of our centers of excellence, our therapeutic centers of excellence. We have 15 of those serving the provider space. That allows us to get very close to those provider relationships across our covered footprint. Within the specialty pharmacy, then we win on consumer experience. We recently won the Specialty Pharmacy of the Year from the National Association of Specialty Pharmacy, an incredibly competitive award. That puts us in the right place to serve consumers as we continue to expand that footprint. This offering is resonating with our PBM clients who look for seamless extension of the specialty pharmacy care as part of their pharmacy benefit.

passages.heading: Patrick, Optum Executive
passages.text: Patrick, Optum Executive: Maybe just two quick other notes on biosimilars, because you asked about that. We're seeing robust uptake across our clients, at the lowest net cost. Our Optum specialty distribution, which we had stood up, is functioning well. Last thing I'll call out: across Krista's and John's teams, really great collaboration between the Optum Health clinicians and the pharmacies to make sure we're providing that integrated care experience for the patients we serve.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Thank you. Next question.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: We'll take our next question from Erin Wright with Morgan Stanley.

passages.heading: Erin Wright, Analyst
passages.text: Erin Wright, Analyst: Great. Thanks. As you continue to make progress on the Optum Health turnaround, I guess how should we think about Optum Health margins, where they land in 2027 relative to that 6%-8%? Just longer term, how you think about potential margins exceeding even that range? Are there any structural constraints to further margin expansion, and with the evolution of that business, the business mix, alongside what you're doing with automation and AI, I guess, could that support even higher margins over time? Thanks.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Before Krista gets to that, maybe just a general comment. There's only so much we can say about 2027. We will have a conversation with you before the end of the year where we'll be able to give you, let's say, more color on 2027, which we view very positively, but we've already provided probably more forward-looking views than we probably have ever done on a call at this stage. With that, I think there's a very positive outlook. Krista, might you want to respond?

passages.heading: Krista, CEO, Optum Health
passages.text: Krista, CEO, Optum Health: Yeah, thanks, Steve, and thanks, Erin, for the question. Again, I think just kind of anchoring back to the work we've been doing to reposition this business for long-term success. Again, really pleased with the performance we're seeing inside 2026. The third quarter is another great example of that. That core performance improvement is durable and will contribute meaningfully to our outlook in 2027. Again, I think 2027 is a year where we'll see a strong pace toward that 6%-8% by 2028. That is really our focus. As I alluded to in the earlier question, I'm optimistic and see a lot of opportunities for growth in this business across the domains I mentioned. But again, I look forward to unpacking more detail around those. I see some of that starting in 2027, but also opportunity in 2028 and beyond for this business across those three domains I mentioned.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Yes. So very positive, but we can't really get to precision at this range. Next question, please.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Andrew Mok with Barclays.

passages.heading: Andrew Mok, Analyst
passages.text: Andrew Mok, Analyst: Hi, good morning. Optum Health's EBIT guidance still appears to imply a meaningfully negative fourth quarter. Can you walk through what's driving that sharp seasonality and help quantify Q4 investments that might be impacting that segment? Thanks.

passages.heading: Krista, CEO, Optum Health
passages.text: Krista, CEO, Optum Health: Yeah. Thanks for the question. I mentioned the third-quarter performance will be durable into the fourth quarter, but the fourth quarter does reflect risk seasonality, which is normal course for this business, and some additional investments that we are making for long-term performance. So inside those additional investments, think of things like technology and AI, but more specifically, even workflow improvements for our clinicians to ensure that we are providing the appropriate expanded access that we are focused on, but also making it easier to care for our patients to deliver strong quality outcomes and support that integrated experience that we are talking about. So think of things like AI-enabled care summaries to make it easier for clinicians to prepare for visits. Ambient—we have talked a lot about how that can translate from just listening and documentation to kind of next-best-action insights for our clinicians. Also, we're doing quite a bit of work on scheduling, as I mentioned. And there is a handful of other investments that we are making in our clinician workflows, again, really just to enable durable performance for the long term in this business. And those are the things that are really part of the fourth quarter. I would say, overall, again, third-quarter performance will be kind of durable into the fourth quarter, but some performance impact is reflected with our risk seasonality. Thanks.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Okay. Thank you. Next question.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: We will take our next question from Matthew Gillmor with KeyBanc.

passages.heading: Matthew Gillmor, Analyst
passages.text: Matthew Gillmor, Analyst: Hey, thanks. I wanted to follow up on some of the policy items that Tim Noel referenced. I think you talked about your work with CMS on quality efforts. You have also talked about the issues on the IDR side. I am just hoping you could give us a sense for how you would like to see those programs evolve over the next few years in a way that would be constructive to the system. Thanks.

passages.heading: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare
passages.text: Tim Noel, CEO, UnitedHealthcare: Yeah. Thanks, Matthew, for the question. With respect to the IDR process, we are really referring to the dispute resolution process. The spirit of the legislation is one that we are certainly aligned on, but the results and outcomes that we are seeing, where the awards are significantly more—multiple times, 10 or 11 times what Medicare would pay in some of those instances—are excessive, and they are contributing to the lack of affordability in healthcare that we are seeing right now. So our issue with the IDR process relates specifically to the dispute resolution and the inefficiencies of it, the cost associated with it, and the outcomes that it is resulting in generating. But not with the spirit of the law, because that is something that we are totally aligned with. And I will turn it over to Bobby to talk a little bit about some of the modernization of the Medicare program.

passages.heading: Bobby, Medicare Executive
passages.text: Bobby, Medicare Executive: Yeah, thanks, Tim. Matthew, and you alluded to it, but we are very appreciative of the active and ongoing dialogue that we have with CMS and with policymakers. What I want you to hear from us is we are supportive of modernization. We are supportive of reform that advances the program and ensures sustainability of the program. We have provided ideas in that regard. Think of quality opportunities, payment opportunities, affordability opportunities, administrative efficiency, and tech interoperability, all in response to CMS's various requests for proposals. I think it is important to note that MA has a really strong foundation from which to build upon, and so it is key that as we pace through these reforms and modernization opportunities, it is done thoughtfully and with broad stakeholder engagement. And that doesn't just mean plans like UnitedHealthcare. That means providers, clinicians, members, broader stakeholders, et cetera. All those voices are critical to this conversation, and it all needs to be done with program stability at the forefront. I am optimistic about what that looks like. Thanks for the question.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Thank you. Next question, please.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Ryan Langston with TD Cowen.

passages.heading: Ryan Langston, Analyst
passages.text: Ryan Langston, Analyst: Great, thank you. You recently talked about making some unique investments in the Stars program. Now that the details are out, I am sorry if I missed this, but can you give us any insight into the size and maybe types of investments you are making in the Stars program? Any commentary you can provide on your broker strategy heading into open enrollment would be helpful as well. Thank you.

passages.heading: Bobby, Medicare Executive
passages.text: Bobby, Medicare Executive: Hey, Ryan. Bobby here. I will hit the Stars one, and then I will hit the broker one quickly as well. Overall, very pleased with how we executed on the controllables for this Star season. We take a long-term view of quality, no different than our approach to products and pricing. While we knew there could be some Star pressure related to the repositioning of benefits we did for 2026 in response to the funding and policy headwinds impacting the overall industry, that is also why we made the investments we did to drive improvements in key areas like clinical outcomes and pharmacy outcomes. What you saw is we actually, year over year, improved nearly every HEDIS and Rx measure for this Star season. But we are not satisfied there. There is more work to be done. There is more opportunity. There's more opportunity to invest and further improve as we pace forward, and that is what we're focused on in that regard. Think of our continued investment in 2026, Q4, and into 2027 as continuing to accelerate, not slow down, given the criticality of quality and Stars to the overall business. Maybe lastly, just your question on brokers. I would say again, similar to my comments around the product positioning, we are more dynamic, really more strategically positioned for 2027 than perhaps in recent years, with key growth opportunities in the D-SNP, C-SNP, and HMO space. We have aligned our broker strategies accordingly. We've aligned our marketing strategies

passages.heading: Bobby, Medicare Executive
passages.text: accordingly, and we are going to market with that very clear objective: to drive good stability within our base business and good growth opportunity in those areas where we think there's some nice opportunity for us. Thanks for the question.

passages.heading: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Steve Hemsley, Chairman and CEO: Thank you. I think we will appreciate the questions this morning and the level of engagement. I think we'll close this now, but we will be around as a team for the rest of the day if you have questions that didn't get responded to or if you have further questions. Again, we thank you for your time today. I hope you get a sense of the momentum we're bringing into 2027, as our emphasis on discipline, execution, and very much improved patient and care provider experiences continues to go forward. I think we'll just build on this quarter by quarter, and we look forward to providing you with a more complete outlook. We'll meet before the end of the year to really engage with investors and give more color on 2027. But thank you, and have a great day.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: This does conclude today's conference. We thank you for your participation, and have a great day.

# UnitedHealth Beats Q3 2026 Earnings and Raises Outlook

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/unitedhealth.svg)

****Key Takeaways****

· UnitedHealth beat Q3 forecasts and raised 2026 profit guidance.

· Lower medical costs boosted margins despite falling membership.

· Rising costs and regulatory risks remain key challenges for 2027.

UnitedHealth Group beat Wall Street third-quarter 2026 forecasts on the 13th of October and raised its full-year profit outlook for the third time this year.1 Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) came in at $4.69 against a $4.12 consensus, and 2026 guidance now stands at no less than $20.50.1 Here's what drove the beat, what changed, and what it could mean for UNH investors.

****UnitedHealth Q3 2026 at a Glance****

· **Earnings beat:** adjusted EPS of $4.69 vs $4.12 expected; revenue of $112.7 billion vs $111.0 billion.1

· **Margin recovery:** the medical care ratio fell to 88.4% from 89.9%, helped by $610 million of reserve releases.1

· **Guidance raised:** 2026 adjusted EPS of at least $20.50, up from $19.50–$20.00.1

· **Weak spot:** members fell to 48.3 million from 50.1 million a year earlier.

· **Stock reaction:** shares have risen more than 7% after brokers lifted targets.

This was a margin-recovery quarter, not a growth quarter. Revenue actually slipped 0.4% year on year as UnitedHealthcare shed members on purpose. But earnings from operations jumped 52% to $6.6 billion, and the repair job that began after the 2025 collapse is now visible in every segment.1

****UnitedHealth Q3 2026 Earnings Are Up 61% Amid Easing Medical Costs****

Adjusted EPS rose 61% to $4.69 from $2.92, while GAAP EPS climbed to $4.56 from $2.59. Net margin nearly doubled to 3.6% from 2.1%.1 Net earnings attributable to shareholders reached $4.1 billion, up from $2.3 billion a year earlier.2

The important medical care ratio (MCR) is at 88.4%, below analyst forecasts.3 Management credited cost management, benefit cuts and pricing discipline. However, the quarter included $610 million of favourable prior-period reserve development for 2026 dates of service, which flattered the ratio.1 The operating cost ratio also improved to 12.8% from 13.5%.1

![](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/image/leverage_shares:037880d21094b-528192be5e64cdc23f306a7783d81949-resized.webp)

Optum Health is the standout turnaround. Revenue fell 10% as the unit exited value-based care markets where it lacked scale, yet operating earnings rose almost eighteen-fold to $735 million.1 Optum Rx benefited from biosimilar adoption, although adjusted scripts dropped to 393 million from 414 million.1

The soft spot was membership. UnitedHealthcare served 48.3 million people, below the 48.6 million analysts expected and down from 50.1 million a year ago.2 Medicare Advantage enrolment has contracted by 935,000 since year-end 2025. Cash flow from operations was $5.1 billion, or 1.2x net income.1

****Why the Medical Care Ratio is Important for UNH Stock****

The medical care ratio (MCR) shows how much of each premium dollar UnitedHealth spends on patient care. At 88.4%, about 88 cents of every dollar went on medical costs, leaving the rest for running costs and profit.

Small moves matter at this scale. On roughly $87 billion of quarterly premiums, a one-point drop in the MCR frees up close to $0.9 billion of profit before tax.1 That is why investors watch this one number more closely than revenue.

**UnitedHealth Raises 2026 Earnings Guidance**

The strongest signal from the report was the improved full-year outlook. UnitedHealth raised its forecast for 2026 adjusted earnings to at least $20.50 per share, up from its previous range of $19.50 to $20.00. The revised target also exceeded the analyst consensus of approximately $19.86 before the announcement.1

![](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/image/leverage_shares:037880d21094b-1eac1db7735b3a4a0e92866056fe3126-resized.webp)

The raise is cautious in shape. Nine-month adjusted EPS already stands at $18.30, so the floor implies only about $2.20 for the fourth quarter. That leaves room for typical Q4 seasonality in Optum Health, plus extra technology spending, which management flagged on the call. It also leaves room for another upside surprise in January.

Capital returns remain intact. The company bought back $5.0 billion of stock and paid $6.2 billion of dividends through September. Debt-to-capital was 41.7%, against a target of about 40% by year-end.1

****What Changed at UnitedHealth in Q3?****

**Commercial medical costs remain the main pressure point.** UnitedHealthcare CEO Tim Noel said commercial cost trend is running above the company's initial 11% assumption, driven by specialty drugs, higher clinician costs and No Surprises Act arbitration. He conceded this pushes out the timeline for long-term commercial margin targets and stressed that the trend is stabilising, not accelerating. Employer attrition also cost 165,000 members in the quarter.1

**Medicare Advantage: smaller, but more profitable.** The deliberate shrink-to-profit strategy continues, with 935,000 fewer MA seniors since year-end 2025.1 According to executives Medicare margins should end 2026 near the top of the 2-4% target range.

**Medicaid is still a drag.** Core Medicaid margins should improve only to modestly better than −1% for 2026, with a return to target margins aimed for 2028.

**Optum Health's repair is ahead of schedule.** Leaving sub-scale value-based care markets lifted the margin to 3.2%, against a 6-8% target for 2028. Optum Insight's AI-driven Integrity One platform has grown from two live clients at the end of 2025 to 15, with 24 more in progress.

**Reputation and regulatory reset.** Management is cutting 30% of prior-approval volume by end-2026, has launched a fee-based, transparent PBM model and plans 100% rebate pass-through by January 2028.1 It is also rebating 2026 ACA individual-market profits to about 1 million members. The Justice Department legal actions over UnitedHealth's Medicare business remain an unresolved overhang.

**UNH Stock Forecast 2027: What Do Analysts Expect?**

The Street's verdict is constructive: most large brokers kept buy-equivalent ratings and several raised targets after the print. CFO DeVeydt said the low end of the 13–16% long-term EPS growth target is a reasonable starting point for 2027 and hinted that consensus may understate the opportunity. Applied to the $20.50 floor, 13% growth implies roughly $23.15 of 2027 adjusted EPS, above the $22.61 consensus. A fuller 2027 outlook is due before year-end.

![](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/image/leverage_shares:037880d21094b-1d40899d1e22a86eb205ceed76fabd3f-resized.webp)

The bull case rests on margin repair. Morgan Stanley argues that the UnitedHealthcare-Optum combination is hard to copy and that cost normalisation should pull margins back toward historical levels.4 Goldman Sachs, per a published summary of its note, sees further profit leverage in Optum Health, commercial and Medicaid.5 Piper Sandler values the shares at 18x estimated 2028 EPS.6 At about 17x forward earnings, the stock trades below its own history.

The bear case is about growth and quality. Membership keeps shrinking, and the stock is down roughly 10% over three months even as rivals held steady. The Q3 MCR beat leaned on $610 million of reserve releases, which will not repeat on schedule. Commercial cost trend, Medicaid funding, Star ratings and the DOJ investigation are the swing factors for 2027.

UnitedHealth has now beaten and raised three times in 2026, and the profit recovery looks durable. The next catalyst is the full 2027 outlook due before year-end, where investors will want proof that earnings can grow even while enrolment does not.

All material contracts between Humana and CMS relating to our Medicare products have been renewed for 2026, and all of our product offerings filed with CMS and going to market for 2026 have been approved.
CMS uses a risk-adjustment model that adjusts premiums paid to Medicare Advantage, or MA, plans according to health status of covered members. The risk-adjustment model, which CMS implemented pursuant to the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 (BBA) and the Benefits Improvement and Protection Act of 2000 (BIPA), generally pays more where a plan's membership has higher expected costs. Under this model, rates paid to MA plans are based on actuarially determined bids, which include a process whereby our prospective payments are based on our estimated cost of providing standard Medicare-covered benefits to an enrollee with a "national average risk profile." That baseline payment amount is adjusted to account for certain demographic characteristics and health status of our enrolled members. Under the risk-adjustment methodology, all MA plans must collect from providers and submit the necessary diagnosis code information to CMS within prescribed deadlines. passages.heading: 2026 Highlights
passages.text:
ality
Our Medicare benefit costs rise as members pay their contractual portion of claims responsibility, progress through their annual deductible and maximum out-of-pocket expenses, as well as incurring higher episodic cost of care resulting in a higher benefit ratio throughout the year.
Our quarterly Insurance segment earnings and operating cash flows are impacted by the Medicare Part D benefit design and changes in the composition of our stand-alone PDP membership. The Medicare Part D benefit design results in coverage that varies as a member’s cumulative out-of-pocket costs pass through successive stages of a member’s plan period, which begins annually on January 1 for renewals. The benefit design changes associated with the implementation of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, or IRA, reduced out-of-pocket costs for beneficiaries, resulting in greater cost sharing and a leveling of net prescription costs throughout the year. In addition, the number of low income senior members as well as year-over-year changes in the mix of membership in our stand-alone PDP products affects the quarterly benefit ratio pattern.
The Insurance segment also experiences seasonality in the operating cost ratio as a result of costs incurred in the
second half of the year associated with the Medicare marketing season.

# Elevance Health Inc (ELV) (Q3 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Raised Guidance, Strong Medicaid and Medicare Advantage Performance, and 12% EPS Growth Outlook for 2027

## Elevance Health Inc (ELV) beat Q3 2026 expectations with $6.99 adjusted EPS, raised its 2026 guidance to at least $29, and reaffirmed confidence in at least 12% adjusted EPS growth for 2027.

![Author's Avatar](https://avatar.gurufocus.com/1_big.png)

GuruFocus News

10/21/2026 19:01

[+ GuruFocus.com on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=gurufocus.com)

![Article's Main Image](https://static.gurufocus.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=600,quality=100/logos/0C000009MT.png?5)

[Click here to view more ELV transcripts](/stock/ELV/transcripts)

[Search All Transcripts and SEC Filings](/search/transcripts)

* **Adjusted Diluted EPS:** $6.99 in Q3 2026, exceeding outlook; includes ~$0.50/share operating outperformance and $1.85/share net nonoperating benefit.
* **2026 Adjusted Diluted EPS Guidance:** Raised to at least $29.
* **2026 Earnings Baseline:** Raised by $0.75 to at least $26.75.
* **2027 EPS Growth Outlook:** At least 12% adjusted diluted EPS growth from the higher baseline.
* **Operating Revenue:** Increased just under 1% to $50.4 billion, driven by higher premium yields, Carelon Rx product revenue and service fees, offsetting lower health plan membership.
* **Medical Membership:** Approximately 44.9 million members; commercial fee-based growth offset anticipated Medicaid attrition.

* **Benefit Expense Ratio:** 90.6%, an improvement of 70 basis points.
* **Adjusted Operating Expense Ratio:** Increased 90 basis points to 11.3%, reflecting targeted onetime investments.
* **Medicaid:** Q3 ahead of outlook on recent rate actions; full year operating margin expected slightly ahead of prior outlook; 2026 viewed as margin trough with improvement expected in 2027.
* **Medicare Advantage:** Full year operating margin of at least 2%; ~half of MA members in plans rated 4 stars or higher; enterprise-wide average of 4 stars.
* **Individual ACA:** Modestly higher full year operating margin on favorable claims; expected to end year with at least 1.2 million members.
* **Commercial Group:** Cost trend consistent with pricing assumptions; pricing discipline maintained through 2027 selling season.
* **Carelon:** Strong quarter; expected contribution to enterprise earnings to grow as programs launch and mature.
* **Days in Claims Payable:** 44.9 days as of September 30, up 3.5 days year-over-year.
* **Operating Cash Flow:** $1.3 billion in the quarter; full year guidance raised to at least $6.5 billion.
* **Cost Savings Initiative:** Elevate platform identified more than $300 million in anticipated savings this year.

Release Date: October 21, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the [full earnings call transcript](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9134756/q3-2026-elevance-health-inc-earnings-call-transcript).

* Elevance Health Inc [ELV](/stock/ELV/summary) raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $29 and increased its 2026 earnings baseline to at least $26.75, reflecting strong operating outperformance.
* The company remains confident in delivering at least 12% adjusted EPS growth in 2027, driven by margin improvement, Carelon expansion, and operating efficiency.
